package_info.why_malicious: The Log4j package contained a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228, 'Log4Shell') that allowed attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems by manipulating log messages. This flaw enabled attackers to gain initial access, deploy malware, establish remote shells, and perform further exploitation, making the package a high-severity risk in any unpatched deployment.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a log message is processed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes a log message containing a JNDI lookup string, which causes Log4j to perform a remote lookup via LDAP, download and deserialize attacker-controlled data, and execute arbitrary code on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input to trigger remote code execution via network-based JNDI lookups, which is highly dangerous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging libraries should never interpret log message content as executable code or perform network lookups based on log data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups are legitimate in controlled, internal environments for service discovery, but not for arbitrary user-supplied input.
key_indicators: Network connection to attacker-controlled LDAP server
Deserialization and execution of remote code

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup string to a vulnerable application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the log message and initiates a remote JNDI lookup.

attack_chain.action: Log4j performs a network request to the attacker-controlled LDAP server specified in the JNDI string.
attack_chain.leads_to: The server responds with malicious Java class data.

attack_chain.action: Log4j deserializes and executes the attacker-supplied code, granting remote code execution on the server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control of the system, can deploy malware, establish persistence, or exfiltrate data.

behavioral_signatures: Log messages containing ${jndi:ldap://...} or similar patterns
Unexpected outbound LDAP, RMI, or DNS requests from application servers
Deserialization of remote Java classes during log processing
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable Log4j versions (2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1)
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP/RMI/DNS requests to untrusted or external IPs/domains
Connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure following log events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for suspicious JNDI lookup patterns, scan for vulnerable Log4j versions, and alert on unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI/DNS traffic from servers. Use SBOMs to identify Log4j dependencies and prioritize patching or mitigation. Employ runtime application security monitoring to detect exploitation attempts.
